study type: Individual Participant Data (IPD) Meta-analysis of cohort studies
exposure: Hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDP) in an index pregnancy
Concomitant HELLP syndrome in index pregnancy
Delivery of a small-for-gestational-age child in index pregnancy
Decreasing gestational age at delivery in the index pregnancy
outcome: Recurrence of hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDP)
Delivery of a small-for-gestational-age child with recurrent HDP
Maximum diastolic blood pressure (in recurrent HDP)
Use of oral antihypertensive medication (in recurrent HDP)
Use of anticonvulsive medication (in recurrent HDP)
cohort: The study included 99,415 women from 22 cohort studies who experienced hypertensive disorders of pregnancy in an index pregnancy and had a subsequent pregnancy.
finding: The recurrence rate of hypertensive disorders in a subsequent pregnancy is relatively low (20.7%), and for most women with recurrent disease, the course of the disease is milder compared to the index pregnancy.
followup_time: Until a subsequent pregnancy and beyond for chronic hypertension, but no specific duration in years is mentioned.
